pack.title: Apologizing well
pack.description: Real repair in one breath. Name it, own it, don't perform it.

scenarios.setting: Coffee with a friend. You forgot their birthday completely.
scenarios.jab: So… you forgot. Everyone else remembered.

replies.line: I forgot, and I'm sorry. Dinner's on me this week.
replies.why: Own it, apologize once, then repair with a plan — in that order.
replies.delivery: Say “I forgot” without an excuse; listen before offering a repair you can honor.

replies.why: No excuses attached — the cleanest apology is the shortest one.
replies.delivery: Say “My fault” clearly, then stop instead of adding a defense. Listen before offering a repair you can honor.

replies.line: I'm really sorry — you deserved better from me. Let me make it up properly.
replies.why: It centers their feeling, not your guilt, then moves straight to repair.
replies.delivery: Keep “I'm really sorry” warm and unhurried; finish the request clearly. Listen before offering a repair you can honor.

trap.line: I'm sorry, but I've just been SO busy lately.
trap.why: It replaces a specific request with accusation, resentment, or an excuse, making your actual boundary less clear.

scenarios.goal: Own a missed birthday and offer a real repair.

followUp.jab: Dinner doesn't undo how it felt.
followUp.line: You're right; I'm sorry I forgot, and I want to hear how it affected you.
followUp.why: It recognizes that a gesture does not erase the hurt and makes space for their experience.
followUp.delivery: Say “I forgot” without an excuse; listen before offering a repair you can honor.

scenarios.setting: Work. You snapped at a junior in a meeting yesterday.
scenarios.jab: Hey — are we okay after yesterday?

replies.line: I snapped at you, and I'm sorry. That wasn't fair.
replies.why: It owns the behavior without deciding whether the other person feels repaired.
replies.delivery: Use a low, sincere tone and pause for their response; do not ask them to reassure you.

replies.line: I snapped. I'm sorry; that wasn't fair.
replies.why: It names the action and apologizes without an excuse.
replies.delivery: Use a low, sincere tone and pause for their response; do not ask them to reassure you.

replies.line: I'm sorry I snapped yesterday; you didn't deserve that, and I want to hear how it affected you.
replies.why: It takes responsibility and makes room for the person's experience.
replies.delivery: Use a low, sincere tone and pause for their response; do not ask them to reassure you.

scenarios.goal: Apologize for snapping without deciding the other person's feelings.

followUp.jab: It made me afraid to ask questions.
followUp.line: I'm sorry; that was my responsibility, and I want you to be able to ask freely.
followUp.why: It owns the impact instead of declaring the relationship repaired on the other person's behalf.
followUp.delivery: Use a low, sincere tone and pause for their response; do not ask them to reassure you.

scenarios.setting: You interrupted a friend and they tell you they felt dismissed.
scenarios.jab: You didn't let me finish what I was saying.
scenarios.goal: Repair an interruption and return the floor.

replies.line: I interrupted you. I'm sorry. Please finish.
replies.why: It owns the action and immediately gives the other person their turn.
replies.delivery: Say the apology once, stop talking, and let the person actually finish.

replies.line: You're right. Please finish; I'll listen.
replies.why: It corrects the immediate behavior rather than extending a defense.
replies.delivery: Say the apology once, stop talking, and let the person actually finish.

replies.line: I'm sorry I cut you off; I want to hear the rest, and I'll wait.
replies.why: It pairs an apology with the changed behavior the conversation needs.
replies.delivery: Say the apology once, stop talking, and let the person actually finish.

followUp.jab: You do that a lot, though.
followUp.line: I hear you; I'll pay attention to that pattern, and right now I want to listen.
followUp.why: It acknowledges the repeated impact without requiring forgiveness before changing behavior.
followUp.delivery: Say the apology once, stop talking, and let the person actually finish.
